q-2615.name: Question 1
q-2615.worked_solution:
Let $u=1-x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=-\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that
$x=1-u.$

Now we can solve the integral in terms of $u,$ and then express our final answer in terms of $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int {x}^{2}\sqrt{1-x}\,\text{d}x & =-\int (1-u)^{2}\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\int ({u}^{2}-2u+1)\sqrt{u}\,\text{d}u \\  & =-\int ({u}^{5/2}-2{u}^{3/2}+{u}^{1/2})\,\text{d}u \\  & =-(\frac{2}{7}{u}^{7/2}-\frac{4}{5}{u}^{5/2}+\frac{2}{3}{u}^{3/2})+C \\  & =-\frac{2}{7}\sqrt{(1-x)^{7}}+\frac{4}{5}\sqrt{(1-x)^{5}}-\frac{2}{3}\sqrt{(1-x)^{3}}+C\end{aligned}
$$

q-49530.problem: Given that $u=x+3$, which integral is equivalent to $\int x\sqrt[4]{x+3}\,\text{d}x?$
q-49530.worked_solution:
Since $u=x+3$, then we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=1\,⟹\,\text{d}x=\text{d}u.
$$

We also note that
$x=u-3.$

Now we can rewrite the integral in terms of $u:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int x\sqrt[4]{x+3}\,\text{d}x & =\int (u-3)(\sqrt[4]{u})(\text{d}u) \\  & =\int (u-3)({u}^{1/4})\text{d}u \\  & =\int ({u}^{5/4}-3{u}^{1/4})\text{d}u\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

Given that u=x+3, which integral is equivalent to ∫xx+34dx?

a
∫3u1/4du
b
∫(u1/4−3u−1/4)du
c
∫(u5/4+3u1/4)du
d
∫(u5/4−3u1/4)du
e
∫u5/4du
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since u=x+3, then we have dudx=1⟹dx=du.

We also note that x=u−3.

Now we can rewrite the integral in terms of u:

∫xx+34dx=∫(u−3)(u4)(du)=∫(u−3)(u1/4)du=∫(u5/4−3u1/4)du
